analysis:
All three files are documentation-only (docs/developer/test.md, docs/provider/cache-storage.md, docs/provider/cli-reference.md). No source, key handling, auth, or wire changes were supplied, so no security regression is shown.

cache-storage.md (head line 88) documents `prefix_cache_status detail=key_unavailable`. It says that when the persistent cache key cannot be loaded, the provider serves uncached. That matches T-041's statement that SSD construction is disabled when the KEK is unavailable, and it is fail-closed. The code behind it is not in the supplied evidence.

cli-reference.md (head lines 17-60) adds the GLM local qualification section and a GLM wired-residency env var (line ~1695). Claims to verify in later passes:
- The encrypted SSD prefix store defaults on for the GLM model, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. This is consistent with the T-041 default-on posture with per-donation gating. The GLM model's cache identity covers the execution policy.
- Image rows get no prefix reuse.
- Video input arrives as an inline data:video URL. T-050 covers earlier plaintext exposure of inline video in provider temp files. The docs do not say how GLM video decode handles temp files, so source review should confirm that plaintext does not reach the filesystem.
- DARKBLOOM_EXPERIMENTAL_GLM5_NEXT is documented as never advertised to the coordinator and not forwarded into launchd, which is a sound boundary claim. The implementation is not supplied.

test.md covers test procedures, including DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR (a test-only selector with canonical absolute path and symlink refusal), App Attest resume, logout and worker tests, and the instruction never to use production cache roots or keys. No threat assumption is invalidated. The T-053, TB-011 and A-008 test references are consistent with the model.

No threat-model update appears needed from these documentation edits alone.
